S.FORM: pai, kinemnemanga tiamadju tu kemacu tua ljigim nua kakinan.
S.PHON: pai kinəmnəmaŋa tiamaɉu tu kəmaʦu tua ʎigim nua kakinan
S.FORM: pai, kinemnemanga tiamadju tu kemacu tua ljigim nua kakinan.
S.PHON: pai kinəmnəmaŋa tiamaɉu tu kəmaʦu tua ʎigim nua kakinan
S.TRANSL: Now, they decided to take their mother's sewing needles.

W.TRANSL: discourse filler, indicating a new topic
decided or thought of, actor focus
sewing needles or box of sewing needles

S.FORM: pai, inika makakiqadilj tia marekaka tua kipaula tua culjan.
S.PHON: pai inika makakiqadiʎ tia maRəkaka tua kipauɣa tua ʦuʎan
S.FORM: pai, inika makakiqadilj tia marekaka tua kipaula tua culjan.
S.PHON: pai inika makakiqadiʎ tia maRəkaka tua kipauɣa tua ʦuʎan
S.TRANSL: Now, the two brothers can no longer take the suffering and hunger.

W.TRANSL: discourse filler, indicating change of topic
tolerate, bear. The root isqadilj'bear, tolerate'.
subject case marker for people, plural

S.FORM: pai, paquzipanga nua kina a kaka a tjaljaljak tua kama niamadju.
S.PHON: pai paquzipaŋa nua kina a kaka a caʎaʎak tua kama niamaɉu
S.FORM: pai, paquzipanga nua kina a kaka a tjaljaljak tua kama niamadju.
S.PHON: pai paquzipaŋa nua kina a kaka a caʎaʎak tua kama niamaɉu
S.TRANSL: It comes to that they are raised by aunt, their father's younger sister.

W.TRANSL: it comes to that, a discourse filler
to raise, feed. The root isquzip'feed, raise', -anga'change of state'.
GEN, marking the agent of the action

S.FORM: pai
S.PHON: pai
S.FORM: pai
S.PHON: pai

TRANSL.notes: Restored from the live source after frozen-scrape review.

S.TRANSL: thus, hence, thereupon, consequently, accordingly, as a result

W.TRANSL: look, thereupon, filler to initiate a new topic

S.FORM: pai, samalji a ku salasaladj tua patjara mavuca a caucau.
S.PHON: pai samaʎi a ku saɣasaɣaɉ tua pacaRa mavuʦa a ʦauʦau
S.FORM: pai, samalji a ku salasaladj tua patjara mavuca a caucau.
S.PHON: pai samaʎi a ku saɣasaɣaɉ tua pacaRa mavuʦa a ʦauʦau
S.TRANSL: Thereupon, my classmates are curious about blind people.

W.TRANSL: look, thereupon, filler to initiate a new topic
to be surprise, actor focus. The root ismalji'different, weird, special'.
partners, friends, classmates, colleagues. The root issaladj'partner'in RED which indicates plural.
blind, actor focus.ma- 'to be in the condition of'; the root isvuca'blind, cannot see'.

S.FORM: namadraudraw aken a kemacu tua ku bintu. pai numayan tjakanauanga ku bintu.
S.PHON: namaɖauɖaw akən a kəmaʦu tua ku bintu pai numajan cakanauaŋa ku bintu
S.FORM: namadraudraw aken a kemacu tua ku bintu. pai numayan tjakanauanga ku bintu.
S.PHON: namaɖauɖaw akən a kəmaʦu tua ku bintu pai numajan cakanauaŋa ku bintu
S.TRANSL: I forgot to bring my lunch box. come, in that case, let's eat my lunch box.

S.FORM: bulai a vaik itjen a ljemangui? bulai aravac. pai, ari vaiki.
S.PHON: buɣai a vaik icən a ʎəmaŋui buɣai aRavaʦ pai aRi vaiki
S.FORM: bulai a vaik itjen a ljemangui? bulai aravac. pai, ari vaiki.
S.PHON: buɣai a vaik icən a ʎəmaŋui buɣai aRavaʦ pai aRi vaiki
S.TRANSL: Is it a good idea that we go swimming? That's very good. Come, let's go.

S.FORM: qemudjaljanga. inika aken a nakemacu tua kausua. maqati aken a supasedjaman? ita a ku kausua. pai, kadjadjalani a kiljaung.
S.PHON: qəmuɉaʎaŋa inika akən a nakəmaʦu tua kausua maqati akən a supasəɉaman ita a ku kausua pai kaɉaɉaɣani a kiʎauŋ
S.FORM: qemudjaljanga. inika aken a nakemacu tua kausua. maqati aken a supasedjaman? ita a ku kausua. pai, kadjadjalani a kiljaung.
S.PHON: qəmuɉaʎaŋa inika akən a nakəmaʦu tua kausua maqati akən a supasəɉaman ita a ku kausua pai kaɉaɉaɣani a kiʎauŋ
S.TRANSL: It's raining now. I did not bring an umbrella. Can you lend me yours? I only have one umbrella. Come, let's share the umbrella.

W.TRANSL: it is raining already, actor focus. The root isqudjalj'rain'.
you lend. The root issedjam'borrow, lend'.
I am not sure about this word.

S.FORM: aicu djukap nua vavui. pai, aicu avan a djaladjalan nua vavui.
S.PHON: aiʦu ɉukap nua vavui pai aiʦu avan a ɉaɣaɉaɣan nua vavui
S.FORM: aicu djukap nua vavui. pai, aicu avan a djaladjalan nua vavui.
S.PHON: aiʦu ɉukap nua vavui pai aiʦu avan a ɉaɣaɉaɣan nua vavui
S.TRANSL: This is the footprints of wild boars. So, this is the path of wild boars.

W.TRANSL: little trail or path. The root isdjalan'road' in RED, smaller road.

S.FORM: pai, iljavaranu. anemanema kudamunu i Taiwan?
S.PHON: pai iʎavaRanu anəmanəma kudamunu i taiwan
S.FORM: pai, iljavaranu. anemanema kudamunu i Taiwan?
S.PHON: pai iʎavaRanu anəmanəma kudamunu i taiwan
S.TRANSL: Come, tell. What fruits are there in Taiwan?

S.FORM: vuvu vavayan, ti kuliu 'a ti paljai amen. pai, suqeljevi amen.
S.PHON: vuvu vavajan ti kuɣiu ʔa ti paʎai amən pai suqəʎəvi amən
S.FORM: vuvu vavayan, ti kuliu 'a ti paljai amen. pai, suqeljevi amen.
S.PHON: vuvu vavajan ti kuɣiu ʔa ti paʎai amən pai suqəʎəvi amən
S.TRANSL: Grandma, it's kuliu and paljai. Please open the door for us.

W.TRANSL: subjet case marker for specific noun
subjet case marker for specific noun
you open the door, imperative inclusive, agent of a Paiwan NAF clause. The root isqeljev'open the door'.
we, 1st person PL Nom, patient of a Paiwan NAF clause

S.FORM: pai, qiladju. anema su'anen?
S.PHON: pai qiɣaɉu anəma suʔanən
S.FORM: pai, qiladju. anema su'anen?
S.PHON: pai qiɣaɉu anəma suʔanən
S.TRANSL: Come, sit down. What will you have?

W.TRANSL: sit, imperative exclusive. The root isqiladj- 'sit, seat'.

S.FORM: pai, kusualapav a dengec i tua su mudingan.
S.PHON: pai kusuaɣapav a dəŋəʦ i tua su mudiŋan
S.FORM: pai, kusualapav a dengec i tua su mudingan.
S.PHON: pai kusuaɣapav a dəŋəʦ i tua su mudiŋan
S.TRANSL: Come, let me get the crumbs off your face.

S.FORM: pai, kipapaulingavu. akumayanga sa su tjengez?
S.PHON: pai kipapauɣiŋavu akumajaŋa sa su cəŋəz
S.FORM: pai, kipapaulingavu. akumayanga sa su tjengez?
S.PHON: pai kipapauɣiŋavu akumajaŋa sa su cəŋəz
S.TRANSL: Come on, get it all together. Why are you dozing off like this?

W.TRANSL: be careful, watch out, keep alert. The root islingav'time, wisdom, hurry'.
for what, why. I think this is a combination of aku 'why',maya'like this or similar', and -anga'suffix indicating change of state'.

S.FORM: pai, mayanan maya penurpur a su kaka.
S.PHON: pai majanan maja pənuRpuR a su kaka
S.FORM: pai, mayanan maya penurpur a su kaka.
S.PHON: pai majanan maja pənuRpuR a su kaka
S.TRANSL: Do not yet disturb your brother.

W.TRANSL: disturb, actor voice. The root ispurpur'annoy, disturb'.

S.FORM: pai, maya manu semannekaaravac tua zuma.
S.PHON: pai maja manu səmannəkaaRavaʦ tua zuma

FORM.notes: Source prints the segmentation seman-neka-aravac. Per POL-014/015 the markers belong on the W and M tiers, so the standard tier drops them; the original keeps the source surface.

S.FORM: pai, maya manu seman-neka-aravac tua zuma.
S.PHON: pai maja manu səmannəkaaRavaʦ tua zuma
S.TRANSL: Do not act like so disrespectful to other people.

W.TRANSL: to excessively disregard or disrespect too much, literally to make nothing out of at all. Interesting word!

S.FORM: pai, kiumalju. semiaq sa su sikudan.
S.PHON: pai kiumaʎu səmiaq sa su sikudan
S.FORM: pai, kiumalju. semiaq sa su sikudan.
S.PHON: pai kiumaʎu səmiaq sa su sikudan
S.TRANSL: Come, change to a new leaf. What you did is shameful.

W.TRANSL: be shameful, actor voice. The root issiaq'shame'.

S.FORM: ljaljeqeljeqel aicu a kinsa. pai, seljecuanan.
S.PHON: ʎaʎəqəʎəqəɣ aiʦu a kinsa pai səʎəʦuanan
S.FORM: ljaljeqeljeqel aicu a kinsa. pai, seljecuanan.
S.PHON: ʎaʎəqəʎəqəɣ aiʦu a kinsa pai səʎəʦuanan
S.TRANSL: The food is already cold. Go, heat it.

W.TRANSL: cold, in RED. The root is ljaljeqel 'cold'.
this. I always thinkaicuisa-icu; however, Professor Anna Chang said it isaicu, and in Paiwan demonstratives and case marker are "mutually exclusive" (Chang, 1992, p. 88).
heat the food.seljecu'heat food by steam'.

S.FORM: pai, pasazalemani a remasudj tua tjakinepel a qavai. ulja tjen a kemeljang tu pidanga supu a penuljat.
S.PHON: pai pasazaɣəmani a Rəmasuɉ tua cakinəpəɣ a qavai uʎa cən a kəməʎaŋ tu pidaŋa supu a pənuʎat
S.FORM: pai, pasazalemani a remasudj tua tjakinepel a qavai. ulja tjen a kemeljang tu pidanga supu a penuljat.
S.PHON: pai pasazaɣəmani a Rəmasuɉ tua cakinəpəɣ a qavai uʎa cən a kəməʎaŋ tu pidaŋa supu a pənuʎat
S.TRANSL: Come, let's put all long rice cakes in line on the floor. We want to know how many there are in total.

W.TRANSL: let's place on the floor, imperative, inclusive. The root iszaleman'floor'.
to make peace. It means to arrange or line up the rice cakes in a good way.
know, actor focus. The root is keljang

S.FORM: pai, kesau tua tjacengelj.
S.PHON: pai kəsau tua caʦəŋəʎ
S.FORM: pai, kesau tua tjacengelj.
S.PHON: pai kəsau tua caʦəŋəʎ
S.TRANSL: Go make our lunch.

W.TRANSL: cook, imperative, exclusive. The root iskesa'cook'.

S.FORM: pai, capau azua vasa.
S.PHON: pai ʦapau azua vasa
S.FORM: pai, capau azua vasa.
S.PHON: pai ʦapau azua vasa
S.TRANSL: Go roast those taros.

W.TRANSL: roast or bake, imperative, exclusive. The root iscapa'roast, bake'.

S.FORM: pai, senasenayu. masepelj itjen.
S.PHON: pai sənasənaju masəpəʎ icən
S.FORM: pai, senasenayu. masepelj itjen.
S.PHON: pai sənasənaju masəpəʎ icən
S.TRANSL: Come, sing a song. We are bored.

W.TRANSL: sing, imperative for the hearer. The root issenay'sing, song' in RED; -u'imperative marker excluding the speaker'.
to be bored.ma- 'to be in the condition of without volition'; the root issepelj'play around without a purpose'.

S.FORM: pai, maya qemaluvu a tja kinateveteveljan.
S.PHON: pai maja qəmaɣuvu a ca kinatəvətəvəʎan
S.FORM: pai, maya qemaluvu a tja kinateveteveljan.
S.PHON: pai maja qəmaɣuvu a ca kinatəvətəvəʎan
S.TRANSL: Come on, do not disturb our gathering.

W.TRANSL: mix up or distrub, actor focus. The root isqaluvu'to mix up, distrub'.

S.FORM: maya masepelj a siqunu ni su vuvu, aya aken tjanusun. inika sun a lemang(e)da. pai, mavuciqanga a su lima.
S.PHON: maja masəpəʎ a siqunu ni su vuvu aja akən canusun inika sun a ɣəmaŋəda pai mavuʦiqaŋa a su ɣima
S.FORM: maya masepelj a siqunu ni su vuvu, aya aken tjanusun. inika sun a lemang(e)da. pai, mavuciqanga a su lima.
S.PHON: maja masəpəʎ a siqunu ni su vuvu aja akən canusun inika sun a ɣəmaŋəda pai mavuʦiqaŋa a su ɣima
S.TRANSL: I told you not to play wioth your grandpa's small knife. You didn't listen. Look, your hand is cut.

W.TRANSL: play with or fiddle with. The root issepelj'tease, fool around with without purpose'.
small knife usually used by elders to cut betel nuts apart and add lime
listen or hear, actor focus. The root islang(e)da'listen, hear'.
gets cut.ma- 'to be in the state of, without volition'; the root isvuciq'cut, sever'; -anga'COS'.

S.FORM: maljenguaqanga aza kuang, pai?
S.PHON: maʎəŋuaqaŋa aza kuaŋ pai
S.FORM: maljenguaqanga aza kuang, pai?
S.PHON: maʎəŋuaqaŋa aza kuaŋ pai
S.TRANSL: That gun is ready, right?

W.TRANSL: to already go in the diretion of well.ma- 'to be in the state of without volition';lje- 'to go in the direction of'; the root isnguaq'well'; -anga'COS'.

S.FORM: inika sun narukisasusu tua mareka tjakaka, pai sipavai tua zuma a hiu niamadju.
S.PHON: inika sun naRukisasusu tua maRəka cakaka pai sipavai tua zuma a hiu niamaɉu
S.FORM: inika sun narukisasusu tua mareka tjakaka, pai sipavai tua zuma a hiu niamadju.
S.PHON: inika sun naRukisasusu tua maRəka cakaka pai sipavai tua zuma a hiu niamaɉu
S.TRANSL: You did not take good care of our brothers and sisters, therefore they gave their votes to others.

W.TRANSL: to have often cared for.na- 'PRF';ru- 'frequently';kisasusu'to investigate, to look after' with the root issusu'meaning'.
our brother and sister.tja- 'our, 1st person PL GEN clitic';kaka'brother or sister'.
therefore, consequently, but also can mean look in this context.
vote, must be a loanword since in Paiwan there is no phoneme /h/ but I do not know its origin.

S.FORM: saqetju a ku kaka, manusika inika kasikakituluan.
S.PHON: saqəcu a ku kaka manusika inika kasikakituɣuan
S.FORM: saqetju a ku kaka, manusika inika kasikakituluan.
S.PHON: saqəcu a ku kaka manusika inika kasikakituɣuan
S.TRANSL: My brother is ill, therefore he did not go to school

W.TRANSL: to the school. kakituluan 'the place to learn' with the roottulu'learn, teach'.

S.FORM: pai manasika a i taiwan mavan a ku qinaljan, uta aya aken.
S.PHON: pai manasika a i taiwan mavan a ku qinaʎan uta aja akən
S.FORM: pai manasika a i taiwan mavan a ku qinaljan, uta aya aken.
S.PHON: pai manasika a i taiwan mavan a ku qinaʎan uta aja akən
S.TRANSL: Therefore, Taiwan is my home, so I also say.

S.FORM: naminseg a ljavek, ayatua neka nu vali.
S.PHON: naminsəg a ʎavək ajatua nəka nu vaɣi
S.FORM: naminseg a ljavek, ayatua neka nu vali.
S.PHON: naminsəg a ʎavək ajatua nəka nu vaɣi
S.TRANSL: The sea has calmed down because there is no wind.

W.TRANSL: have become calm.na- 'PRF'; the root isminseg'calm, still'.
? Usuallynuis your (2nd personal plural GEN). Here why the elder saysnuis unknown to me.

S.FORM: kipaula aravac tiamadju ta icu a qudjalj, ayatua siniqaljudj a quma.
S.PHON: kipauɣa aRavaʦ tiamaɉu ta iʦu a quɉaʎ ajatua siniqaʎuɉ a quma
S.FORM: kipaula aravac tiamadju ta icu a qudjalj, ayatua siniqaljudj a quma.
S.PHON: kipauɣa aRavaʦ tiamaɉu ta iʦu a quɉaʎ ajatua siniqaʎuɉ a quma
S.TRANSL: They suffer severely from this rain, because the farm was washed away.

W.TRANSL: suffer from or experience something bad or encounter.ki- 'to get or obtain'; the root ispaula'diaster, pity, experience'.
because or as, provides not the cause but result.
to be swept or washed away. The root isqaljudj'swept or washed away'.

S.FORM: ayatua a picul a ligu nisunanga a penuljat a kemasi tucu a patje palalautanga. amin.
S.PHON: ajatua a piʦuɣ a ɣigu nisunaŋa a pənuʎat a kəmasi tuʦu a pacə paɣaɣautaŋa amin
S.FORM: ayatua a picul a ligu nisunanga a penuljat a kemasi tucu a patje palalautanga. amin.
S.PHON: ajatua a piʦuɣ a ɣigu nisunaŋa a pənuʎat a kəmasi tuʦu a pacə paɣaɣautaŋa amin
S.TRANSL: Because power, honor, all belongs to you, from now until forever. amen.

W.TRANSL: of yours already.ni- 'of, GEN marker'; -sun'you, 2nd person SING clitic'; -anga'change of state COS'.
forever or everlasting. The root ispalalaut'forever'.

S.FORM: inianga kapazangal a kemesa tucu, ayatua izuanga a tinku.
S.PHON: iniaŋa kapazaŋaɣ a kəməsa tuʦu ajatua izuaŋa a tinku
S.FORM: inianga kapazangal a kemesa tucu, ayatua izuanga a tinku.
S.PHON: iniaŋa kapazaŋaɣ a kəməsa tuʦu ajatua izuaŋa a tinku
S.TRANSL: Because of electrical rice cooker, it is no longer difficult to cook now.

W.TRANSL: no longer.ini- 'no, not, NEG'; -anga'marker of change of state'.
electric rice cooker, loanword from Mandarin.

S.FORM: ayatua a benuru uri si'atarivak na 'u lingalingaw.
S.PHON: ajatua a bənuRu uRi siʔataRivak na ʔu ɣiŋaɣiŋaw
S.FORM: ayatua a benuru uri si'atarivak na 'u lingalingaw.
S.PHON: ajatua a bənuRu uRi siʔataRivak na ʔu ɣiŋaɣiŋaw
S.TRANSL: Because exercise will make my body healthy.

W.TRANSL: exercise or do sports or literally to play with a ball, AF. The root isburu'ball', loanword.
to make healthy, IF. The root istarivak'healthy'.

S.FORM: djaljepan a kisasusu aravac tjajuaken a nia sinsi, manu seljaseljang ni kama kisansinsi.
S.PHON: ɉaʎəpan a kisasusu aRavaʦ cajuakən a nia sinsi manu səʎasəʎaŋ ni kama kisansinsi
S.FORM: djaljepan a kisasusu aravac tjajuaken a nia sinsi, manu seljaseljang ni kama kisansinsi.
S.PHON: ɉaʎəpan a kisasusu aRavaʦ cajuakən a nia sinsi manu səʎasəʎaŋ ni kama kisansinsi
S.TRANSL: So that's why my teacher cares very much for me, because he was dad's colleague at school.

W.TRANSL: so that's the way it is; so the reason why...is that...
our, often used in Paiwan even for its singular sense
to be a teacher, teaching at a school

S.FORM: djaljepan tu kemavasun tua bulabulay, avan susikabulay.
S.PHON: ɉaʎəpan tu kəmavasun tua buɣabuɣaj avan susikabuɣaj
S.FORM: djaljepan tu kemavasun tua bulabulay, avan susikabulay.
S.PHON: ɉaʎəpan tu kəmavasun tua buɣabuɣaj avan susikabuɣaj
S.TRANSL: Oh, the reason why you are so beautiful is because of the clothes you're wearing!

W.TRANSL: so that's the way it is; so the reason why...is that...
you wear, AF. The root iskava'shirt, clothes'; -sun'you, clitic'.
the way you use to become beautiful or the reason why you become beautiful, IF

S.FORM: sedjaljepsun a kisankalaingan.
S.PHON: səɉaʎəpsun a kisankaɣaiŋan
S.FORM: sedjaljepsun a kisankalaingan.
S.PHON: səɉaʎəpsun a kisankaɣaiŋan
S.TRANSL: You are suitable for leadership.

W.TRANSL: you are right or suitable for or you have the quality of.se- 'have the quality of'; the root isdjaljep'fit, suitable, assistant'; -sun'you, 2nd person SIN clitic'.
to become a leader.kisan(e)- 'to become or to act as';kalaingan'the elderest, leader' comes fromka-laing-anwith the rootlaing'the elderest, supervise, leadership'.

S.FORM: a kisedjaljep a mayatucusun a makinamalji?
S.PHON: a kisəɉaʎəp a majatuʦusun a makinamaʎi
S.FORM: a kisedjaljep a mayatucusun a makinamalji?
S.PHON: a kisəɉaʎəp a majatuʦusun a makinamaʎi
S.TRANSL: Is it appropriate for you to get so mad like this?

W.TRANSL: to be suitable or appropriate. The root isdjaljep'fit, suitable, assistant'.
to be angry.ma- 'to be in the state of without volition';ki- 'to get or obtain';na- 'PRF'; the root ismalji'different, special, angry or mad'.

S.FORM: uri venli aken tu drusa a djaljeng a nigi. izua a tjelu a djaljeng imaza. nisunaianga a penuljat.
S.PHON: uRi vənɣi akən tu ɖusa a ɉaʎəŋ a nigi izua a cəɣu a ɉaʎəŋ imaza nisunaiaŋa a pənuʎat
S.FORM: uri venli aken tu drusa a djaljeng a nigi. izua a tjelu a djaljeng imaza. nisunaianga a penuljat.
S.PHON: uRi vənɣi akən tu ɖusa a ɉaʎəŋ a nigi izua a cəɣu a ɉaʎəŋ imaza nisunaiaŋa a pənuʎat
S.TRANSL: I want to buy two bunches of green onions. There are three bundles here. They are all yours.

W.TRANSL: buy, AF. The root isveli'buy or sell'.
binding for flowers or hays or leafy vegetables

If we usemalimormadraudraw, the main part of the utterance will bemadjeleanga a malim/madraudrawtuangadan nua caucau. This word also breaks a previously established phonological rule which says Paiwan languages avoids vowel clusters.maalim,madjeleangaare two examples. You hear clearly how two vowels stand next to each other.

He studied the Paiwan language, and helped to change (translate) the Bible and hymns to the Paiwan language, and this began the writing of the Paiwan language.

W.TRANSL: to be able to teach, AV.ma- and <em> 'AV marker';sa- 'wish to'; the root istulu'teach'.
believer, loanword from Japanese 信者 しんじゃ.
someone in the habit of teaching or missionary. The root istjaucikel'story, reason'.
come from, AV. The root iskasi'to be from, come from'.
pastor, loanword from Japanese 牧師 ボクシ.
to be sent to. The root issekaulj'serve, to be a missionary of'.
helped or assisted with.pu- 'to obtain';saladj'companion, partner'.

change, i.e. translate, AV. The root isumalj- 'change, alter'. This is interesting phonologically. When a Paiwan word begins with a verb, the AV form starts withm- likem-alap'to take', but this one starts with the infix <em>. It is reasonable to think there must be a glottal /q/or /k/or /‘/before the infix because infix does not stand in the beginning of a word. Therefore, I added the glottal.
Bible, loanword from Japanese 聖書 せいしょ.
hymns or praise songs, loanword from Japanese 賛美歌 さんびか.
it started already. The root is tagilj 'start'; -anga'COS'.

S.FORM: pai ka 1945 a cavilj, mangetjez a sinzia a krisitu a ciuru kiukai a sema tua qinaljan nua sepaiwan a patagilj. ayatua tjuruvu aravac a caucau a masalu, sa meliyaw a isauniuni a liningedjelj a kiukai.

S.TRANSL: Since the year of 1945, believers of the Christian Presbyterian churchstarted to arrive at the Paiwan villages. Because there were very many people who believed, and the church soon grew very fast.

believers, loanword from Japanese信者しんじゃ.
Paiwan people.se- 'belonging to or coming from a certain place'.
start, for the first time, in the beginning.pa- 'to cause to be'; the root istagilj'start, beginning'.
a lot of, used for people
believe, AV. The root issalu'faith, believe, thank'.

S.FORM: amin a vecik a pasemalaw tua pasasevalivalit, tua penacalivatan na taqaljaqaljan, a papacun tua natemalidu a kakudan nua kacalisiyan, sa tuluwan, sa pazurungan. ljakua neka nu vecik tua kai nua kacalisiyan.

changes.pa- 'to cause to be';sa- andse- 'have the quality of'; the root isvalit'change, replacement' in RED
things that have passed or history, UV. The root iscalivat'pass over'; -an'nominalization'.
to show or present. The root iscun'see'.
exciting or interesting or impressive, AV.na- 'have become'; the root istalidu'appreciate, spectacular'.
continuance or transmission.pa- 'to cause to be'; the root iszurung'push forward'; -an'NMZ'.
this is also very interesting case marker to think further about. Is it a demonstrative for Paiwan? I see it many times functioning as demonstrative before a noun.

W.TRANSL: hill people or indigenous people. The root iscalisi'hill, slope'; -an'specific location in space, referent focus, NMZ'.
coming for a long time ago, AV.kasi'come from';cuai'a long time ago'.
made, UV. The root islang'make';malangmeans to make, AV. The vowel /a/ must be an addition to make the word pronounciable, likelapandm-a-lap'take, AV'.
the thing that is drawn or pattern, UV. The root isvecik'pattern'; /e/ disappears phonologically.
made, UV. The root islang'make';malangmeans to make, AV. The vowel /a/ must be an addition to make the word pronounciable, likelapandm-a-lap'take, AV'.
weave, AV. The root iscepu'weaving'; /e/ disappears phonologically.
the thing that is drawn or pattern, UV. The root isvecik'pattern'; /e/ disappears phonologically.

our (spoken) language.tja- 'our, GEN, proclitic';kai'language, spoken word'.

our ways of life or our culture.ka- 'inchoative marker'; the root iskuda'custom'; -an'NZM'. [Now I am getting curious about-an. This suffix is used a lot and has many functions or meanings.]

S.TRANSL: This tree is the place where we stopped when we came here last time.

W.TRANSL: is, 'be' verb. In the study of Paiwan, the common knowledge is there is no 'be' verb.
the place where rest is taken, i.e. where someone pauses to rest, UV (-in-) plus NMZ (-an). The root issekez'rest, pause'. The vowel /e/ is weakened to disappearance, a phonological rule in Paiwan.

we came here. ka- or ta- 'in past';si- 'belonging to a certain time in the past'; the root isi-maza'here' (i'LOC' + the rootmaza'here'); -an'nominalization of location, NMZ of LOC'; -men'we', fromamen, bound form and overlapped vowel.
before.ka- orta- 'in past'; tjai 'OBL for common noun'; the root issangas'before, previously, first'.

battery, loanword from Japanese でんち 電池.

for me, towards me or with me

? I cannot find this word. sinsi kalekes's translation is like to be found out or give away.

But considering the case marker (AV subject markerarather than UV subject markerni) that follows, I know in this case-em-(AV) prevails -in- (UV).

S.TRANSL: Indigenous rituals are of two kinds. There is one kind for the business of our individual life as human, and there is another kind for the business of the people as a whole like farming or worshipping elders. We celebrate the harvest festival every year, and we celebrate the Five-year Ritual every five years. As we say, everything that we have, our dreams, and our good fortune in life are all given by our elders.

S.TRANSL: When aboriginal children are entering adulthood, the woman priest will bring them to elders who will teach them courage. Boys will be given simple tools, which will be blessed by the woman priest. The next day, the male priest will bring them to the hunting place for them to try hunting. Girls do not have business as hunting. The woman priest will pray to give them courage. When it is done, girls will be see the slaughter of the pig on one day and that concludes the ceremony of everlasting wisdom.
